title:
Comment of Krisitne Sowl in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152137.txt
documents.text:
Krisitne Sowl, Homer, AK.
Thank you for your opportunity to comment. Communities near big development projects should always be allowed to comment. I do not think a huge underwater data center will be beneficial to the people of the Cook Inlet region.
1.	It’s experimental. No one has done such a large project for an underwater data center. And this area seems like a very challenging location to have an experimental data center. Underwater structures are subject to fouling by marine organisms and this is a huge maintenance burden that will not be present on terrestrial data centers. Such a large structure is likely to impact currents and circulation in Cook Inlet that could lead to coastal erosion or sedimentation in unexpected areas. Cook Inlet is extremely turbid and the high sediment load in the water also likely to lead to maintenance issues. Cook Inlet has extreme tidal ranges. If this data center cannot be powered during extreme low tides, then it will be a vampire on our terrestrial power grids, exacerbating our already rising power costs.
2.	Its proposed location is in an ecologically sensitive area. They are choosing to put a huge data center in the bottleneck between Upper and Lower Cook Inlet. This will impact shipping traffic to and from the port of Anchorage. It will provide a barrier for endangered beluga whales moving between their calving grounds in upper Cook Inlet and seasonal feeding areas in Lower Cook Inlet. And the noise will also have a huge impact on our small beluga population. Salmon is king in Alaska. It is an important food resource for humans and wildlife, as well as being an important economic resource for the State. A huge data center could interfere with salmon migration. All the excess heat produced by the data center is likely to harm salmon and all other marine resources. 
3.	Once again, outside interests are planning to suck up all the profits at the expense of Alaskans’ resources. Delaware is a coastal state. Why don’t they build their data center there?
